Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class Relation<R extends Model,S extends Relation<R,S>>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.Relation<R,S>
Type Parameters:
R - the related model class
S - the relation's own class
Direct Known Subclasses:
BelongsTo, BelongsToMany, HasOneOrMany, HasOneOrManyThrough, MorphTo
public abstract class Relation<R extends Model,S extends Relation<R,S>> extends Object
A relation between a parent model and the related model class: Laravel's Eloquent Relation, with HasOne, HasMany and BelongsTo as its kinds.

A relation is built unconstrained. The public query members (getQuery(), get(), getResults() and the clause forwarders) add the relation's lazy constraints once, before their own work, so post.comments().get() reads the post's comments. Eager loading and whereHas reach the relation through package-private hooks that never add them. That is how Laravel's static Relation::$constraints switch is replaced: no flag shared between threads, and each path says which constraints it wants.

A relation instance is single use and not safe to share across threads. Build a new one, through the model's typed method or relation(name), for each query.

Users write the concrete type, such as HasMany<Comment>; S is the relation's own class, so the forwarders return it. Only this package defines relation kinds.

    • touch

      public void touch()
      Sets the update timestamp of every related row this relation reads to now, in one raw UPDATE over the lazy query: no select, no events, no casts. Laravel's Relation::touch.

      Nothing runs when the related class keeps no timestamps (including inside Model.withoutTimestamps(java.util.function.Supplier<R>)), has no update timestamp column, or has its touches switched off on this thread by Model.withoutTouching. The value is the related model's own Model.freshTimestampValue(): its clock and stored form, the same text or Instant an ordinary save of that model writes, whatever the parent's clock is.

      Throws:
      QueryException - if the database refuses the update

    • rawUpdate

      public final int rawUpdate(Map<String,?> attributes)
      Runs an UPDATE of the given columns over the lazy query, with the clauses added to this relation. No model is read or saved: no events, no casts, no timestamps.
      Parameters:
      attributes - the columns and their new values, never null or empty; values are bound as given
      Returns:
      the number of rows changed
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if attributes is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if attributes is empty or a value is a list, map or array
      QueryException - if the database refuses the update
